passages.text: We must pay closer attention, therefore, to what we have heard, so that we do not drift away.
passages.sermon:
We have heard the message of salvation from the Lord.
This message is very important.
We must pay close attention to what we have heard.
If we do not pay attention, we may drift away from the truth.
passages.original: Διὰ τοῦτο δεῖ περισσοτέρως προσέχειν ἡμᾶς τοῖς ἀκουσθεῖσιν μή‿ ποτε παραρυῶμεν

passages.text: For if the message spoken by angels was binding, and every transgression and disobedience received its just punishment, how shall we escape if we neglect such a great salvation? This salvation was first announced by the Lord, was confirmed to us by those who heard Him, and was affirmed by God through signs, wonders, various miracles, and gifts of the Holy Spirit distributed according to His will.
passages.sermon:
God sent messages through angels in the past.
These messages were binding.
Every act of disobedience or breaking of these messages received a just punishment.
God is just.
God punishes every transgression and disobedience.
We now have a great salvation.
The Lord Jesus first announced this salvation.
People who heard Jesus confirmed this message to us.
God also affirmed this message.
God gave signs to show the truth of this salvation.
God performed wonders and various miracles.
God gave gifts of the Holy Spirit.
God distributed these gifts according to His will.
If we neglect this great salvation, we cannot escape judgment.
passages.original: εἰ γὰρ ὁ δι’ ἀγγέλων λαληθεὶς λόγος ἐγένετο βέβαιος καὶ πᾶσα παράβασις καὶ παρακοὴ ἔλαβεν ἔνδικον μισθαποδοσίαν πῶς ἡμεῖς ἐκφευξόμεθα τηλικαύτης ἀμελήσαντες σωτηρίας ἥτις ἀρχὴν λαβοῦσα λαλεῖσθαι διὰ τοῦ Κυρίου ὑπὸ τῶν ἀκουσάντων εἰς ἡμᾶς ἐβεβαιώθη συνεπιμαρτυροῦντος τοῦ Θεοῦ σημείοις τε καὶ τέρασιν καὶ ποικίλαις δυνάμεσιν καὶ Πνεύματος Ἁγίου μερισμοῖς κατὰ τὴν αὐτοῦ θέλησιν

passages.text: For it is not to angels that He has subjected the world to come, about which we are speaking.
passages.sermon: God did not put the world to come under the authority of angels.\r\nWe are speaking about this future world.\r\nGod chose not to subject it to angels.
passages.original: Οὐ γὰρ ἀγγέλοις ὑπέταξεν τὴν οἰκουμένην τὴν μέλλουσαν περὶ ἧς λαλοῦμεν

passages.text: But somewhere it is testified in these words: “What is man that You are mindful of him, or the son of man that You care for him?
passages.sermon:
God created all things.
God rules over all things.
Someone once spoke these words about people.
He said, “What is man that You remember him?”
He also said, “What is the son of man that You care for him?”
God thinks about people.
God cares for people.
God pays attention to the son of man.
passages.original: διεμαρτύρατο δέ πού τις λέγων Τί ἐστιν ἄνθρωπος ὅτι μιμνῄσκῃ αὐτοῦ ἢ υἱὸς ἀνθρώπου ὅτι ἐπισκέπτῃ αὐτόν

passages.text: You made him a little lower than the angels; You crowned him with glory and honor and placed everything under his feet.” When God subjected all things to him, He left nothing outside of his control. Yet at present we do not see everything subject to him.
passages.sermon:
God made man a little lower than the angels.
God crowned man with glory and honor.
God placed everything under man’s feet.
God subjected all things to man.
God left nothing outside of man’s control.
Right now, we do not see everything subject to man.
passages.original: ἠλάττωσας αὐτὸν βραχύ τι παρ’ ἀγγέλους δόξῃ καὶ τιμῇ ἐστεφάνωσας αὐτόν πάντα ὑπέταξας ὑποκάτω τῶν ποδῶν αὐτοῦ Ἐν τῷ γὰρ ὑποτάξαι αὐτῷ τὰ πάντα οὐδὲν ἀφῆκεν αὐτῷ ἀνυπότακτον νῦν δὲ οὔπω ὁρῶμεν αὐτῷ τὰ πάντα ὑποτεταγμένα

passages.text: But we see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels, now crowned with glory and honor because He suffered death, so that by the grace of God He might taste death for everyone.
passages.sermon:
We see Jesus.
God made Jesus a little lower than the angels.
Jesus suffered death.
God crowned Jesus with glory and honor because of His suffering.
By God's grace, Jesus tasted death for everyone.
passages.original: τὸν δὲ βραχύ τι παρ’ ἀγγέλους ἠλαττωμένον βλέπομεν Ἰησοῦν διὰ τὸ πάθημα τοῦ θανάτου δόξῃ καὶ τιμῇ ἐστεφανωμένον ὅπως χάριτι Θεοῦ ὑπὲρ παντὸς γεύσηται θανάτου

passages.text: In bringing many sons to glory, it was fitting for God, for whom and through whom all things exist, to make the author of their salvation perfect through suffering.
passages.sermon:
God exists as the one for whom all things exist.
God exists as the one through whom all things exist.
God brings many sons to glory.
God made Jesus the author of their salvation.
God made Jesus perfect through suffering.
This was fitting for God.
passages.original: Ἔπρεπεν γὰρ αὐτῷ δι’ ὃν τὰ πάντα καὶ δι’ οὗ τὰ πάντα πολλοὺς υἱοὺς εἰς δόξαν ἀγαγόντα τὸν ἀρχηγὸν τῆς σωτηρίας αὐτῶν διὰ παθημάτων τελειῶσαι

passages.text: For both the One who sanctifies and those who are sanctified are of the same family. So Jesus is not ashamed to call them brothers.
passages.sermon:
Jesus sanctifies people.
He makes them holy.
The people He sanctifies are called the sanctified.
Jesus and the sanctified come from the same source.
They belong to the same family.
Because of this, Jesus is not ashamed of them.
Jesus calls them His brothers.
passages.original: ὅ τε γὰρ ἁγιάζων καὶ οἱ ἁγιαζόμενοι ἐξ ἑνὸς πάντες δι’ ἣν αἰτίαν οὐκ ἐπαισχύνεται ἀδελφοὺς αὐτοὺς καλεῖν

passages.text: He says: “I will proclaim Your name to My brothers; I will sing Your praises in the assembly.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the One who sanctifies.
Jesus calls those He sanctifies His brothers.
Jesus says, “I will proclaim Your name to My brothers.”
Jesus also says, “I will sing Your praises in the assembly.”
passages.original: λέγων Ἀπαγγελῶ τὸ ὄνομά σου τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς μου ἐν μέσῳ ἐκκλησίας ὑμνήσω σε

passages.text: And again: “I will put My trust in Him.” And once again: “Here am I, and the children God has given Me.”
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the One who sanctifies.
He and those He sanctifies are from the same family.
Jesus is not ashamed to call them brothers.
Jesus says, “I will put My trust in Him.”
Jesus also says, “Here I am.”
He says, “Here are the children God has given Me.”
passages.original: Καὶ πάλιν Ἐγὼ ἔσομαι πεποιθὼς ἐπ’ αὐτῷ Καὶ πάλιν Ἰδοὺ ἐγὼ καὶ τὰ παιδία ἅ μοι ἔδωκεν ὁ Θεός

passages.text: Now since the children have flesh and blood, He too shared in their humanity, so that by His death He might destroy him who holds the power of death, that is, the devil, and free those who all their lives were held in slavery by their fear of death.
passages.sermon:
The children are human.
They have flesh and blood.
Jesus also became human.
He shared in flesh and blood like the children.
Jesus did this so He could die.
By His death, Jesus could destroy the one who has the power of death.
The one who has the power of death is the devil.
Jesus did this to set people free.
These people were slaves all their lives.
They were slaves because they feared death.
passages.original: Ἐπεὶ οὖν τὰ παιδία κεκοινώνηκεν αἵματος καὶ σαρκός καὶ αὐτὸς παραπλησίως μετέσχεν τῶν αὐτῶν ἵνα διὰ τοῦ θανάτου καταργήσῃ τὸν τὸ κράτος ἔχοντα τοῦ θανάτου τοῦτ’ ἔστιν τὸν διάβολον καὶ ἀπαλλάξῃ τούτους ὅσοι φόβῳ θανάτου διὰ παντὸς τοῦ ζῆν ἔνοχοι ἦσαν δουλείας

passages.text: For surely it is not the angels He helps, but the descendants of Abraham.
passages.sermon:
Jesus helps people.
He does not help angels.
He helps the descendants of Abraham.
The descendants of Abraham are people chosen by God.
Jesus gives help to them.
passages.original: Οὐ γὰρ δή‿ που ἀγγέλων ἐπιλαμβάνεται ἀλλὰ σπέρματος Ἀβραὰμ ἐπιλαμβάνεται

passages.text: For this reason He had to be made like His brothers in every way, so that He might become a merciful and faithful high priest in service to God, in order to make atonement for the sins of the people.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
Jesus became like His brothers in every way.
His brothers are human beings.
Jesus shared fully in humanity.
He did this for a reason.
He wanted to become a merciful high priest.
He wanted to become a faithful high priest.
He serves God as high priest.
He makes atonement for the sins of the people.
He removes the sins of the people by His work.
passages.original: ὅθεν ὤφειλεν κατὰ πάντα τοῖς ἀδελφοῖς ὁμοιωθῆναι ἵνα ἐλεήμων γένηται καὶ πιστὸς ἀρχιερεὺς τὰ πρὸς τὸν Θεόν εἰς τὸ ἱλάσκεσθαι τὰς ἁμαρτίας τοῦ λαοῦ

passages.text: Because He Himself suffered when He was tempted, He is able to help those who are being tempted.
passages.sermon:
Jesus is the Son of God.
Jesus became like us in every way.
Jesus suffered when He was tempted.
Jesus understands our struggles.
Jesus is able to help people who are being tempted.
passages.original: ἐν ᾧ γὰρ πέπονθεν αὐτὸς πειρασθείς δύναται τοῖς πειραζομένοις βοηθῆσαι
